newInput: How does caching work in Redis?

answersA.title: How caching works in Redis
answersA.text: Caching in Redis works by storing frequently accessed data in memory, which allows for much faster retrieval than disk-based storage. When a request comes in, Redis first checks its in-memory cache. If the data is found (a cache hit), it's returned immediately. If not (a cache miss), Redis fetches the data from the primary data store, returns it to the client, and also stores a copy in its cache for future requests. This significantly speeds up read operations for popular data.

newInput: Back to hash tables, how do you handle collisions?

answersA.title: Hash table collision handling
answersA.text: A hash table collision occurs when two different keys hash to the same index. Common methods to handle this include separate chaining and open addressing. Separate chaining stores colliding elements in a linked list at that index. Open addressing probes for the next available slot in the table itself, using strategies like linear probing, quadratic probing, or double hashing.
